units.title: Kubernetes reconciliation mental model
units.objective: Explain Kubernetes as API objects plus controllers that repeatedly compare desired and observed state, and locate the first control-plane and node responsibilities without claiming internals mastery.

exercise.summary: Given a fixed Deployment, ReplicaSet and Pod fixture plus two observed snapshots, identify desired state, observed state, controller responsibility and the next observation needed without running a mutation.

project_task.summary: Construct a deterministic paper/simulated reconciliation trace and distinguish scheduler placement from controller convergence and kubelet execution.

acceptance: Desired state, observed state and reconciliation are explained using the supplied objects rather than slogans.
API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, kubelet and container runtime responsibilities are separated at an introductory level.
The trace does not claim that a controller executes containers or that the scheduler maintains replica count.
Unknown component internals are recorded as later study instead of guessed.

triggers: Kubernetes stable documentation moves beyond v1.36
Core component or controller semantics used by the unit change
Learner evidence exposes a missing prerequisite

limitations: Content readiness and a completed diagram do not prove learner mastery.
The unit does not cover etcd operations, scheduler algorithms, controller source code, HA or production control-plane operation.

units.title: Read-only discovery, diagnosis and evidence
units.objective: Collect bounded Kubernetes observations, separate facts from hypotheses and produce a redacted evidence report using only declared read-only commands against a disposable fixture environment.

exercise.summary: Against a prebuilt disposable failure fixture, use only get, describe, logs and events observations to produce a timestamped report; do not repair or mutate the cluster.

project_task.summary: Diagnose one bounded Pod scheduling or startup symptom through an observation chain and stop at the first unsupported conclusion.

acceptance: Environment, Kubernetes/kubectl versions, fixture identity and observation timestamps are recorded.
Every executed command is in the read-only allowlist and the report records that no repair was attempted.
Facts, hypotheses and unverified explanations are clearly separated and sensitive output is redacted.
A second run over the same fixture produces the same normalized evidence apart from declared volatile fields.
The learner identifies what the evidence does and does not prove.

triggers: Kubernetes or kubectl stable moves beyond v1.36
Selected read-only command output semantics change
A fixture reveals an unsafe or ambiguous command boundary

limitations: Passing a deterministic fixture does not prove learner mastery or production-cluster diagnosis competence.
No mutation, root-cause repair, live production access, CNI/CSI deep dive or HA diagnosis is included.
